claims.note_on_random_guess: g64 (24.17%) and g128 (24.83%) fall below the 25% random-guess line; g32 (25.17%) does not. The three are within 1 point of each other, so this is a boundary case, not a separation between granularities.

limits: One checkpoint, one 600-item C-Eval validation slice, one run per granularity.
The quantiser is per-group absmean simulated in float32: accuracy only, no speed or memory claim.
g32 came from a run that was cut short by a wall-clock limit before the other granularities; its integers are recorded from that run's log rather than recomputed by this script.
Three granularities overlapping does not prove granularity is irrelevant above 32 - only that it is not distinguishable in this range at this depth.

protocol.readout: mean log P(option tokens | question + options), divided by token count
protocol.why: the published cost table used a letter-argmax readout that scores below a constant-answer baseline on this checkpoint; this re-measures the cost with the readout that clears it
